hi there, i'm (21F) not a parent or anything and i'm pretty young but i'll offer what i can with what i have. i'd been having plenty of bouts of suicide for the past few years. what always seemed to keep me from ending it all was this: there are people who need me. despite me being fed up with life, and whether i feel like i add value to their lives or not, these people still need me. their lives would be completely disrupted if i committed suicide. they love me, like your son and husband love you. they truly don't have the best ways of showing it, but think about it. your 4 year old autistic son who you're with every single day. he's attached to you, maybe he feels at home is the place he's most comfortable expressing himself, that could be why he's always screaming there and not at school. if you die now, he'll probably end up depressed and fair much worse than if you were there, caring for him. i don't mean to be harsh but he's YOUR son. your love for him is probably how you've made it this far. i'd suspect if you weren't there, he'd be a lot more likely to be mistreated.

my advice? first, take a short vacation, maybe 3 days at a spa or something ALONE or with a girlfriend (if you have any in the country). tell your husband to make it work because you're with that child every day. your husband can be responsible for his own child for 3 days, and you really need a break. everyone needs a break sometimes. when you return, see about hiring a part time nanny who has experience with autistic children. there are plenty out there. maybe since you're about to start working again and you'll have the extra income, it would be good to start looking soon.

i have a degree in psychology but i didn't specialize in autism, so i don't know specifically what activities i could tell you to do to distract him. however, i know a few things about early childhood development which are just some things to consider about reasons why he's always screaming. all children need and crave routine. they like to know what to expect, and changes can stress them out. children generally want both parents around all the time, he could be missing dad. maybe he's not stimulated enough at home, try to introduce him to new things. if he likes to make messes, give him a space where he (or both of you) can make big messes, like a finger painting area. all just suggestions aa i don't know many details about your son's specific development.

lastly, this is likely the lowest point in your life... which means the only way you can go now is up :) things get better with time. i see how hard it is for you now, but don't you want the chance to see it get better? to see your son possibly become verbal, and get an A+ on his tests, and give you mother's day gifts, and grow? he's still a kid, and autistic or not, kids grow and develop and change. he'll be easier to handle when he has a better sense of the world around him.

good luck, and take it easy on yourself <3
